facts.fact: The World Bank ID4D diagnostic, conducted in 2016 with UNDP and IOM, states that Somalia's civil records are not digitised and that verification is manual, from paper records where these exist; it puts under-five birth registration at about 3 per cent (7 per cent in Somaliland), citing UNICEF 2013.

The World Bank ID4D diagnostic of 2016 states that civil registration is completely decentralised, with some of the country's 22 municipalities charged with keeping registers and issuing birth, death and marriage certificates, and that civil records are not digitised, verification resting on paper records where these exist.

The World Bank ID4D diagnostic of 2016 states that civil records are not digitised in a system run by some of the country's 22 municipalities, whose implementation it calls poor and uneven; it gives no count of registration offices and names no office entering records digitally.
